fix(demos): align MemoryFileSystem.dirname with node:path + correct stale comment

[LAW:types-are-the-program] MemoryFileSystem.dirname diverged from
node:path.dirname for relative inputs — "a", "a/", "a/b", "" all
returned "/" because the `idx <= 0` branch conflated "no slash" with
"slash at position 0". Split the two cases: idx < 0 → "." (relative
parent), idx === 0 → "/" (immediate child of root). The two FileSystem
impls now agree on every relative-path edge case node:path covers.

New tests pin parity with node:path.dirname for the five relative-path
cases: "", "a", "a/", "a/b", "a/b/c". Pulled the absolute-path tests
into their own block so the parity check is legible as its own concern.

[LAW:comments-explain-why-only] (suppressed Copilot finding, no thread)
The extractUuid comment claimed it "falls back to JSON.parse" but the
implementation has been regex-only — comment was inherited from an
earlier draft and never updated. Rewrote to describe what the code
actually does (regex-only by design; false positives tolerable because
downstream falls back to opening at line 0).

Addresses Copilot review round 8 on PR #47.

docs(demos): correct MemoryFileSystem path doc + fixture key hint

[LAW:comments-explain-why-only] The MemoryFileSystem header said paths
are "always absolute", but join/basename/dirname all accept relative
inputs and tests rely on that — claim was wrong. Reworded to describe
the actual behavior (slash-separated; both absolute and relative
supported; tree lookup always works in absolute terms under `home`).

The embedded session fixture hinted at `r` to toggle raw view, but
keymap.ts maps `v` to toggle-view-mode. Updated the fixture text.

Addresses Copilot review round 7 on PR #47.

fix(demos): derive empty-state path from fs; correct wire.ts quit comment

[LAW:one-source-of-truth] The empty-state status message hardcoded
"~/.claude/projects/" but the actual root depends on fs.homeDir() and
fs.join — wrong in the browser fixture (/home/demo/.claude/projects)
and on any non-POSIX host. Now derives the displayed path from the
fs capability so the message always reflects the actual root scanned.

[LAW:comments-explain-why-only] The wire.ts catch-handler comment said
the browser "never fires" quit, but keymap.ts maps both `q` and Ctrl-C
to {type:"quit"} and xterm delivers those keystrokes normally. Comment
now says run() can resolve cleanly on quit; the page shell just does
not auto-unmount on that resolve, so the demo sits idle in restored
alt-screen state.

Addresses Copilot review round 5 on PR #47.

docs(demos): describe MemoryFileSystem.lookup resolution rules precisely

[LAW:comments-explain-why-only] The inline comment claimed "any ancestor
of home resolves to the root directory" but the implementation returns
null for filesystem root `/` when home is non-root, and only treats
*non-empty* partial prefixes as synthetic directories. Replaced the
two-clause comment with four explicit resolution rules so the doc
matches behavior.

Addresses Copilot review round 4 on PR #47.

docs(demos): tighten readFirstBytes and scanner header accuracy

[LAW:comments-explain-why-only] The readFirstBytes comment claimed the
returned byte length "matches the requested cap" — but a truncated
multibyte UTF-8 sequence decodes to U+FFFD (3 bytes), which can exceed
the cap. The existing test pins this case. Comment now describes what
actually happens: the *read* is capped at maxBytes; decoding may emit
replacement chars and the returned text's byte length is not strictly
≤ maxBytes, matching node's Buffer.toString.

The scanner header said the first-line peek is "for slug extraction"
but extractMeta() also derives firstPrompt from the same line.
Updated to mention both.

Addresses Copilot review round 3 on PR #47.

fix(demos): track host width live in Console + hoist TextDecoder

[LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow] Console.width falls back to
process.stdout.columns (undefined in browser → 80), causing layout to
render at 80 cols while xterm.js is at 100. Override consoleOut.width
with a live getter that reads host.size().cols — render width tracks
the actual terminal in both environments with no env-branching, and
resize is followed naturally because the getter re-reads on every
access.

Hoist the input-path TextDecoder out of the onData closure so we don't
allocate one per keystroke. Hot path; small savings but right hygiene.

Addresses Copilot review round 2 on PR #47.

fix(demos): byte-precise MemoryFileSystem.readFirstBytes + honest wire.ts catch

[LAW:types-are-the-program] readFirstBytes' contract was `maxBytes` but the
memory impl was character-slicing — that's a hidden divergence from
NodeFileSystem on multibyte input. Memory now encodes via TextEncoder,
slices the byte buffer, and decodes with a non-fatal TextDecoder so both
impls behave identically at the byte boundary (split multibyte → replacement
char, returned byte length never exceeds the cap). New test pins this with
a 4-char/8-byte fixture.

The wire.ts catch handler claimed it would surface boot-time failures to
the page-shell status badge, but mount.ts.tmpl only catches synchronous
mount() throws — an async run() rejection wouldn't update the badge, and
the `.catch(throw)` was creating an unhandled rejection in the browser.
Now: log to console.error + host.stop(), no rethrow. The comment describes
what actually happens, including why we deliberately don't reach into the
DOM shell to update the badge (that would couple wire.ts to the shell's
structure — a separate seam).

Addresses Copilot review on PR #47.

feat(demos): FileSystem capability + claude-sessions browser bundle (rich-demo-site-pek.3.1)

[LAW:capabilities-over-context] Extract a FileSystem capability covering exactly
the operations claude-sessions performs (homeDir, join, basename, dirname,
exists, readDir, stat, readFile, readFirstBytes) and thread it through the
demo. NodeFileSystem wraps node:fs/path/os for the terminal entry;
MemoryFileSystem serves an embedded session fixture for the browser entry.

[LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow] The demo body never branches on environment —
index.ts and wire.ts differ only in which capability instances they construct.
The same run(host, fs) call drives both.

[LAW:single-enforcer] node-file-system.ts is the only file in the demo tree
that touches node:fs/path/os. _capabilities/index.ts deliberately omits
NodeFileSystem so the browser-safe barrel cannot transitively pull node
modules at bundle time.

Console writes now flow through hostStream(host) so the same render path
drives node stdout and xterm.js. Existing node entry (npm run sessions)
behaves identically.

Verified: lint clean, 1736 tests pass, demos:build produces the
claude-sessions bundle, headless-browser gate (8/8) covers it via the
manifest-driven test.

fix(security): strip OSC terminators from link URLs at the trust boundary (rich-strip-render-d5z.2) (#46)

* fix(security): strip OSC terminators from link URLs at the RichText boundary (rich-strip-render-d5z.2)

A URL containing ESC (\x1b), BEL (\x07), or ST (\x9c) bytes could
prematurely terminate an OSC 8 hyperlink wrap and inject arbitrary
terminal control bytes. The fix sanitizes link URLs at the trust
boundary — RichText — without modifying the Style value type.

- Add Style.withLink(link): structural clone helper, mirrors withoutColor.
- Add sanitizeStyleLink in text.ts as a module-private peer to the
  existing stripControlChars, applied at all four RichText inflow points:
  constructor options.style, the style setter, stylize, append.
- Style stays a faithful container; raw new Style({ link }) does not
  sanitize, so internal callers that already sanitized are not silently
  re-mutated.
- Sanitizer is reference-preserving on clean URLs (no needless clone).

[LAW:single-enforcer] [LAW:locality-or-seam] One sanitizer rule, applied
at the boundary the data crosses. Renderer downstream trusts the
invariant and emits without guards.

7 new tests pin the contract end-to-end: markup/stylize/append/
constructor/setter all strip; raw Style does not; rendered output cannot
escape the OSC 8 wrap.

* fix(security): centralize link sanitization in resolveStyle to close bypass paths

Copilot review on PR #46 identified that the original 4-point wrap
(constructor / style setter / stylize / append) missed three other
style-accepting paths: highlightRegex, highlightWords, and the
per-region span re-resolution in _buildSegments. A caller passing
`new Style({ link: dirty })` to any of those produced a span whose
URL bytes could still escape the OSC 8 wrap downstream.

Fix: move sanitizeStyleLink into `resolveStyle` itself — the single
canonical normalizer for `string | Style | undefined → Style` inside
text.ts. Every current and future RichText method that normalizes
a style argument now inherits sanitization structurally; no
per-callsite wrap to forget.

[LAW:single-enforcer] One enforcement point, applied at the
canonicalization boundary. The 4 explicit `sanitizeStyleLink(...)`
wraps at the original sites become plain `resolveStyle(...)` calls —
the rule lives in one place instead of four. The `style` setter is
the only path that doesn't pass through `resolveStyle` (its argument
is already a Style), and continues to call sanitizeStyleLink
directly so the boundary contract holds for every assignment.

[LAW:locality-or-seam] `_buildSegments`' per-region
`resolveStyle(span.style)` call now provides structural enforcement
at the last render-pipeline step before bytes leave RichText — a
stricter placement than per-entry-method sanitization.

3 new tests pin the previously-bypassed coverage:
- highlightRegex sanitizes
- highlightWords sanitizes
- the Segment emitted by render() carries a sanitized URL end-to-end

* fix(security): wire-byte sanitization at OSC 8 emit + extract shared rule

Copilot round 2 on PR #46 was right: the RichText boundary alone leaves
gaps. A Style with a hostile link can still enter the rendering
pipeline without passing through RichText — `Console.print({ style:
new Style({ link: dirty }) })` routes via Segment.applyStyle and
Style.add (both faithful — preserve link verbatim), so the dirty URL
reaches render.ts and escapes the OSC 8 wrap.

Fix: layered enforcement at two distinct seams, sharing one rule.

- Extract `stripOscTerminators` to `src/core/sanitize.ts` — a leaf
  module that depends on nothing, so render.ts, style.ts, and text.ts
  can all import without inverting the dep graph. [LAW:one-source-of-truth]
  the regex lives in exactly one place.

- text.ts: data-model boundary (unchanged behavior, now imports the
  shared helper). Required by the ticket's acceptance criterion that
  "the stored URL has the ESC/ST stripped" — RichText.spans[].style.link
  is sanitized in-memory so inspection matches what the renderer emits.

- render.ts:segmentsToString and style.ts:Style.render: wire-byte
  boundary. The two OSC 8 byte producers in the codebase now both
  pipe the link through `stripOscTerminators` before interpolation.
  Style itself stays a faithful container — only the bytes going out
  the door are sanitized, the in-memory `style.link` is unchanged.

[LAW:single-enforcer] One rule (the regex in sanitize.ts), applied
at every seam the URL crosses. Forgetting to wrap a future API is no
longer possible — wire bytes are always safe regardless of which
upstream path constructed the Style.

[LAW:locality-or-seam] The two layers are not redundant — they cover
distinct seams: in-memory model cleanness (RichText) vs wire-byte
safety (renderer/Style emit). Together they guarantee dirty bytes
neither live in the data model nor escape on the wire.

Updates the over-claiming comment in text.ts to reflect the layered
enforcement (Copilot was right that the prior text implied a global
invariant the rest of the pipeline didn't enforce).

2 new tests pin the wire-byte boundary: a dirty Style handed straight
to segmentsToString or to Style.render — bypassing RichText, markup,
and every input-sanitizing layer — still produces safe OSC 8 bytes.

* docs: update style.ts one-way-deps comment to reflect sanitize.js import

Comment at style.ts:13-16 had become stale after the previous commit
added `import { stripOscTerminators } from "./sanitize.js"`. Update
the dep-direction note to accurately list both `core/color` and the
leaf `core/sanitize` module. Caught by Copilot review on PR #46.

[LAW:one-source-of-truth] LAW: markers are load-bearing claims about
architecture — keeping them accurate is required, not optional.

fix(coverage): label every allowlist entry by its actual export kind

Copilot review on PR #35 flagged that the reason string for KeyEvent
called it a "type" when src/widgets/types.ts declares it as a class.
A reader debugging a coverage failure consumes that reason string
verbatim — a wrong label is misleading guidance, not just imprecision.

The same pattern was repeated across many entries (I had labeled most
interfaces as "type" and several classes as "type"). Rather than
fix only the entry Copilot named, a derivation pass over src/ rewrote
every reason string from the actual export declaration:

  - class      → "<scope>: <Name> class"
  - interface  → "<scope>: <Name> interface"
  - type       → "<scope>: <Name> type alias"
  - const      → "<scope>: <Name> constant"
  - function   → "<scope>: <Name> function"
  - enum       → "<scope>: <Name> enum"

83 lines of labels updated. Existing parenthetical context (e.g.
"used transitively via Pretty") is preserved.

[LAW:one-source-of-truth] The src/ declaration is the canonical
description of an export's kind. A reason string that disagrees with
it is a divergent copy — fix the divergence by deriving from the
source, not by patching the copy point-by-point.

Verification: npm run lint clean; coverage verifier still green
(4/4).

chore(demos): retire flagship-per-domain spec and typing

Removes the artifacts that encoded the over-fit "exactly five flagships
with strict source-module ownership" model the previous demo-tune-up
design produced. The lit epic (rich-demos-l2x) has already been
rewritten back to the user's original ask (dedupe / expand / consolidate
/ reorganize / tweak — fewer + more interesting demos, with existing
working demos preserved until something better replaces them).

# Changes

- **Deleted `spec/demos.md`** — the 392-line spec that defined five
  flagships with rigid source-module ownership and mandated deleting the
  interactive TUIs (rich-explore, claude-sessions) to satisfy the count.
  Retired in favor of judgment-driven concrete improvements.

- **`test/coverage/coverage-allowlist.ts`** — dropped the `Flagship`
  string-literal union, the `burndown(flagship)` helper, and the
  discriminated-union `AllowlistEntry` (`{ kind: "burndown" }`
  vs `{ kind: "permanent" }`). Collapsed to one flat shape:
  `AllowlistEntry { reason: string }`. Per-flagship comment headers
  replaced with factual "-- from src/X --" sectioning. [LAW:absorbed-variance]
  — the discriminated union only had one realized case (burndown);
  collapse to one shape.

- **`test/coverage/coverage.test.ts`** — softened the file header
  comment (no longer claims to be "the keystone" of an epic; explicitly
  notes the verifier is a *floor*, not a quality measure). Updated the
  error messages and the redundant-entry detail to match the new
  AllowlistEntry shape.

- **`examples/themes-and-color-studio/index.ts`** — header comment no
  longer calls the demo "the flagship"; describes what it actually is
  (a printed-tour reference kept for the color subsystem, not a template
  for future demos). One-liner inside main() and one in-line infra
  comment updated to match.

# Verification

- npm run lint: clean
- npx vitest run: 8838 passed | 7 skipped (328 files)
- npm run themes-and-color-studio: runs to completion

# What is NOT changed

No demos under `examples/` are deleted. All existing demos
(`rich-explore`, `claude-sessions`, `rich-themes`, `rich-themes-transposed`,
`rich-theme-designer`, `rich-colors`, `rich-config`, `dropdown-demo`,
`rich-dash`, `rich-markup-plugins`, `rich-strip`, `rich-template-bindings`,
`themes-and-color-studio`, `shared`) remain on disk; their npm scripts
remain wired. Per parent epic non-goal: working demos are not deleted
before something concrete has replaced them and been judged a
replacement.
